Hi Maria — great to meet you and Tom today, appreciate the detailed questions. Below is a concise recap and next steps; I've looped Karthik (security/solutions) and Jordan (AE) for technical details and contracting cadence.

Recap / answers at a glance:
- BAA: Redwood provides a standard BAA for customers processing PHI. We can start with our BAA template and typically turn around an initial draft within 3-5 business days; final execution timeline depends on customer's legal review.
- Eligible hosting for PHI: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments are supported for PHI. Our public hosted multi-tenant API is not eligible for PHI under the standard terms.
- SOC 2: We can share a SOC 2 Type II snapshot for the last 12 months — attaching a sanitized summary.
- Controls: We recommend KMS-backed encryption (customer-managed keys where required), configurable retention policies, and audit logging (exportable to your SIEM). For POC, default retention can be set to 30 days with shorter TTLs available.

Attachments: redwood_soc2-snapshot.pdf (summary), initial BAA template (we'll attach in next message for intake).

Next steps / asks:
1) Karthik to confirm PHI handling boundaries and any service-level constraints for a limited-scope POC.
2) We will share a draft BAA and a simple mutual action plan (timeline + responsibilities).
3) Please confirm expected POC start date window (you mentioned late Oct).
4) If you need, we can schedule a 30-min security-tech deep dive next week.

Thanks — Aisha

Hi Maria — copying the short technical answers here so your security intake has specifics. I also attached an architecture sketch and the draft BAA for your legal team.

Detailed notes: 
- PHI eligibility: only Dedicated (redwood-dedicated) and Private (redwood-private / on-prem) deployments are supported for PHI. The hosted multi-tenant API (redwood-hosted) is explicitly excluded for PHI under our current compliance posture.
- Data flow for POC: we recommend Dedicated with VPC peering or Private VPC for minimal network hops. For an initial limited-scope POC that processes patient names + notes, Dedicated with private networking + KMS-managed keys strikes the best balance for speed to POC and compliance.
- KV cache & inference: We avoid persisting KV cache to long-term storage for PHI workloads. Runtime caching is kept in-memory and scrubbed on session end unless explicitly captured under customer retention settings.
- Retention & logging: Default POC retention = 30 days (can be reduced to 0–7 days). Audit logs are exportable; we can ship logs via S3 to your account or push to your SIEM.
- Encryption: At-rest encryption uses AES-256; encryption keys managed via Redwood KMS or your external KMS (customer-managed keys supported). TLS 1.2+ in transit.
- SOC 2 & evidence: Attached is a redacted SOC 2 summary and a checklist we typically fill for intake. For deeper evidence (control narratives, auditor contact) we can coordinate an NDA if required.

Attachments: redwood_baa-draft.docx, network-architecture-diagram.png

Implementation constraints / SAOs to be aware of:
- Scheduling: Dedicated capacity provisioning (reserved pool) requires a 2–3 week lead time to guarantee GPU SKU and region.
- SLA: For PHI workloads we recommend our Dedicated plan with the optional SLA add-on; Private on-prem deployments will have custom timelines.

If that aligns, Aisha/Jordan will send the mutual action plan and the draft BAA for legal review. Happy to jump on a call with your infosec next week (Wed/Thu mornings PT work for me).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
